content.summary: The additional evening shift finishes the work sooner: completion time improves by 33.2% (delta -33.2%), waiting working time falls by 55.8%, and on-time delivery rises from 65.5% to 100.0%. Output is unchanged at 3,228 stones, but throughput per working hour is slightly lower, and total cost rises by INR 19,118 (+2.2%).
keyChanges: On-time delivery rate improves from 65.5% to 100.0%, with 10 fewer delayed orders.
Total cost rises by +INR 19,117.83 (+2.2%), driven mainly by employee cost (+INR 26,878.13).
Throughput per working hour falls by 1.3 stones per hour (-4.0%), because the working time is longer.
Polishing remains the primary bottleneck, but its mean working wait falls by 56%.
risks: Cost per output stone rises by INR 5.92 per stone, so the extra shift is more expensive per stone.
Polishing wheels are still at 82.1% utilization, so the bottleneck is not removed.
content.bottleneckExplanation: Polishing is still the bottleneck in both runs. Its busiest pool, Polishing wheels, drops from 89.6% to 82.1% utilization in the scenario.

recommendations.title: Pursue the additional shift, after checking its cost against the on-time gain
recommendations.rationale: Delivery performance improves strongly, while cost rises by a small share. Confirm that the cost increase is acceptable for the on-time gain.

recommendations.title: Simulate adding polishing capacity in Scenario Lab
recommendations.rationale: Polishing is still the bottleneck. Create a scenario with more polishing wheels, run it, and compare it with this run.

assumptions: The results depend on the simulated shift, the stated resource capacities and the order list as given.
limitations: Cost increases are based on the simulated employee and machine costs only.
Changes not simulated in this run cannot be assessed from this evidence.

evidence.label: Completion time: difference relative to the baseline
On-time delivery rate: difference (scenario minus baseline)
